c74object.name: ortho
c74object.digest: Invented-language generator — pseudo-words from a seeded language substrate
c74object.description:
ortho mints a language once from a seed and then draws every word from that same invented tongue, so output reads as internally consistent rather than as noise. The same seed always names the same language, on every host and every machine.
Seven dials control how much the language repeats itself and how it is punctuated. Each token comes out with a classification saying why it appeared, so a patch can treat a recurring name differently from a freshly minted word.

inlet.digest: bang, tokens N, page N, section, cleardials, attributes
inlet.description: All input arrives here. Generation messages produce text on both outlets; attribute messages change settings without producing output.

outlet.description: One symbol per word. Walk it with zl or store it with coll.

outlet.digest: sources (0 fresh 1 function 2 topic 3 name 4 phrase)
outlet.description:
One integer per word, aligned position for position with the left outlet. 0 is a freshly generated word; 1 a document-scope function word; 2 a section-scope topic; 3 a section-scope name; 4 a member of a recurring phrase.
Fired before the left outlet, so anything reacting to the words already has the matching classifications available.

method.name: bang
method.description: Produces one paragraph of sentences sentences, each up to max_words words long. Capitalisation, terminal marks, and any punctuation the dials call for are included.

method.name: tokens
method.description:
Produces exactly the requested number of words, with no capitalisation, no terminal marks, and no punctuation of any kind. Recurrence still applies.
This is the conformance path — the one that diffs against the published golden vectors — and the safe path when the words are headed somewhere that treats punctuation specially.

method.name: page
method.description:
Produces the requested number of paragraphs as one continuous token run. The cast of names and topics persists across all of them; only section changes subjects.
Output is capped at 1024 tokens. If a request would exceed that, the object emits what fits and posts a warning saying how many paragraphs it managed.

method.name: section
method.digest: Mint a fresh cast of names, topics, and phrases
method.description: Starts a new section: new names, new topics, new recurring phrases, and any half-delivered phrase is dropped. The language itself does not change — same substrate, new subjects. Produces no output on its own.

method.name: cleardials
method.digest: Zero all seven dials and the preset
method.description: Sets every dial to 0, clears preset to 0, and forgets which dials were set by hand. After this the object is back to its bare default, where every token is freshly generated.

attribute.name: seed
attribute.description:
The seed IS the language. Setting it immediately mints a new substrate, so every word afterwards is drawn from a different invented tongue. The same seed always produces the same language, in this object, in the JavaScript reference, and in the openFrameworks addon.
Range 0 to 4294967295. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: phrases
attribute.description: How often a multi-word phrase recurs. Phrases arrive whole and in order rather than word by word. Tokens drawn from a phrase report source 4. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: function_words
attribute.description: How often the small grammatical glue words recur. These are document-scope: they persist across sections, the way "the" and "of" persist across chapters. Source 1. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: topics
attribute.description: How often the section's subject matter recurs — the words the passage appears to be about. Section-scope: section mints a new set. Source 2. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: names
attribute.description: How often the section's cast of names recurs — the people the passage appears to be about. Section-scope: section mints a new cast. Source 3. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: commas
attribute.description:
How often commas appear, anchored to function words so the pacing falls where a reader expects it. Affects the readable paths only; tokens is never punctuated. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.
A comma is attached to its word, so a token can arrive as one symbol containing a comma. See the discussion below.

attribute.name: quotation
attribute.description: How often a span of direct speech appears, anchored to a name from the current cast so someone in the passage appears to be speaking. Readable paths only. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: scare_quotes
attribute.description: How often a single term is held at arm's length in quotation marks. Readable paths only. Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: preset
attribute.description:
A single knob that fills all seven dials at tuned proportions — a starting point when you do not want to set seven values by hand.
Dials you set yourself are never overwritten by the preset, so order does not matter: [ortho @preset 0.5 @names 0.9] and [ortho @names 0.9 @preset 0.5] produce identical settings. Send cleardials to release every hand-set dial back to the preset's control.
Range 0 to 1, default 0. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: max_letters
attribute.description:
Ceiling on word length, not a target — each word's length is drawn randomly below this value, so words vary. Not a dial: this shapes the output without changing the language.
The paragraph path (bang and page) draws twice: once for a per-sentence ceiling below this value, then once per word below that. Paragraphs therefore run noticeably shorter than tokens at the same setting. Raise this well above the length you want if paragraphs read as too clipped.
Default 8. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: max_words
attribute.description: Ceiling on words per sentence, drawn randomly below this value rather than fixed at it. As with max_letters, the paragraph path draws twice, so sentences run shorter than this number suggests. Not a dial. Default 12. Saved with the patcher.

attribute.name: sentences
attribute.description: How many sentences a bang produces, and how many go into each paragraph of a page. Not a dial. Default 4. Saved with the patcher.

c74object.discussion:
DIALS VERSUS SHAPING. The seven dials are the language: they control recurrence and punctuation, and their names are fixed across every program that speaks ortho. The three shaping attributes (max_letters, max_words, sentences) only control how much text comes out. Changing a dial changes the character of the writing; changing a shaping value changes its size.
PUNCTUATION AND MESSAGE BOXES. With the punctuation dials above zero, a token can arrive as one symbol carrying a comma or quotation marks, such as a word followed by a comma. That symbol travels safely through zl, coll, route, and anything else programmatic. It is only re-read if it is pasted into a message box, because Max treats a comma as a message separator there. Punctuation is deliberately left intact rather than stripped, because it is part of the language and every other ortho host keeps it. Use tokens when you need output guaranteed free of it.
WHERE THE LANGUAGE LIVES. The generator itself is ortho-kernel, a plain C library containing no Max code at all. This object is only a translation layer: it converts tokens into Max symbols and exposes the dials. That is why a seed produces the same words here, in the JavaScript reference implementation, and in the openFrameworks addon — the language is not reimplemented per host, it is shared.
FRESH INSTANCES. Every word drawn advances the generator, so an object that has already produced output is at a different point in the stream. To reproduce a known sequence, use a newly created object and send its generation message first.
